input.question: Why do we urinate even when we are dehydrated/thirsty?
input.ground_truth: Let's start by differentiating between thirsty and dehydration. Thirst is wanting water, dehydration is running out of water. At later stage dehydration your renal system shuts down and waste backs up. You eventually die. You pee because you're using water to get rid of bad stuff in your system, not because you have too much water.

Question: Why do we urinate even when we are dehydrated/thirsty?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a big house, and inside your house, there are lots of tiny workers who need to stay clean and healthy. These workers are your cells.

Now, sometimes you don’t drink water for a while, maybe because you forgot or you’re too busy playing. Your body still needs to keep the house clean, so it makes a little bit of pee (that’s what we call urine) to get rid of things your body doesn’t need.

Even if you’re thirsty and your body wants more water, it still has to clean itself a little bit. That’s why you might still pee, even when you’re thirsty. But if you keep not drinking water, your body will make less pee to save water, so you don’t get too dehydrated.

So, your body always tries to keep the house clean, even when it’s waiting for more water to come in!
